manual.prompt: Use induction to prove that $\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}6$, the sum of the first $n$ squares, is always an integer for positive integers $n$, by showing $6\mid n(n+1)(2n+1)$.

manual.title: Binomial lower bound with a quadratic term
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $(1+x)^{n}\ge1+nx+\dfrac{n(n-1)}2x^{2}$ for all $x\ge0$ and integers $n\ge1$.

manual.title: Power rule for derivatives by induction
manual.prompt: Using the product rule and $\dfrac{d}{dx}x=1$, prove by induction that $\dfrac{d}{dx}x^{n}=nx^{n-1}$ for all integers $n\ge1$.

manual.title: Sum of sines of odd multiples
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $\sin x+\sin3x+\cdots+\sin(2n-1)x=\dfrac{\sin^{2}nx}{\sin x}$ for $n\ge1$, where $\sin x\ne0$.

manual.title: Three to the four n minus one divisible by eighty
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $3^{4n}-1$ is divisible by $80$ for all integers $n\ge1$.

manual.title: Factorial less than n to the n
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $n!<n^{n}$ for all integers $n\ge2$.

manual.title: Repeated derivatives of x e to the x
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that the $n$th derivative of $xe^{x}$ is $(x+n)e^{x}$ for all integers $n\ge1$.

manual.title: Sum of k over factorial k plus one
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac k{(k+1)!}=1-\frac1{(n+1)!}$ for $n\ge1$.

manual.title: Divisibility by twenty four needing a second fact
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $2\cdot7^{n}+3\cdot5^{n}-5$ is divisible by $24$ for all integers $n\ge1$. You may use that $5^{n}-5$ is divisible by $4$.

manual.title: Sum of reciprocal roots at most two root n minus one
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac1{\sqrt k}\le2\sqrt n-1$ for all integers $n\ge1$.

manual.title: Telescoping product of one plus a reciprocal
manual.prompt: Prove by induction that $\left(1+\tfrac11\right)\left(1+\tfrac12\right)\cdots\left(1+\tfrac1n\right)=n+1$ for all integers $n\ge1$.

manual.title: A strengthened induction bound
manual.prompt: Prove by mathematical induction that $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{k^{2}}\le2-\frac1n$ for all integers $n\ge1$. Hence show that the sum is always less than $2$.
hints: Proving "< 2" directly does not induct; the stronger bound does.
Reduce the step to comparing 1/k − 1/(k + 1) with 1/(k + 1)².

ladder.nudge: Proving "< 2" directly does not induct; the stronger bound does.
ladder.method: Reduce the step to comparing 1/k − 1/(k + 1) with 1/(k + 1)².

steps.d: So the sum is at most $2-\tfrac{1}{k+1}<2$
